baseline_models.focus_anchor: The comparison links كَلِمَةٍ at word 2 to شَجَرَةٍ at word 4, repeats خَبِيثَةٍ at words 3 and 5, then predicates total extraction and absence of قَرَارٍ.
baseline_models.mechanism: A meaningful expression is mapped onto a stemmed, rooted organism. Repeating the same bad quality across word and tree makes corruption continuous from message to carrier; extracting the organism from its origin prevents the expression from becoming a durable, self-maintaining presence.

activation_trace.role: The proverbial comparison supplies the mapping frame through which properties of the tree become properties of the word.
A meaningful lexical unit that can widen into a saying or discourse supplies the message that the organic image embodies.
Badness contrary to wholesomeness occurs on both word and tree, making defect systemic rather than an accident of appearance.
The stemmed plant supplies an organism whose visible extension normally depends on an embedded base.
Whole extraction from the origin supplies complete severance rather than pruning or temporary damage.
Fixity and settlement supply the missing capacity that would let the word-tree remain and reproduce its presence.

changed_reading.before: A bad saying is simply compared to an uprooted tree.
changed_reading.after: Bad discourse is pictured as an attempted living carrier whose defect occupies both message and medium, so it cannot maintain an origin-bearing presence.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The branch ranges of كَلِمَةٍ, شَجَرَةٍ, خَبِيثَةٍ, ٱجْتُثَّتْ, and قَرَارٍ permit a social mechanism while remaining attached to words 2-6 and 13.
baseline_models.mechanism: The word can register as a wound, the tree root as entangled dispute and mixed speech, and badness as corruption through bad associates. On this branch-distant reading, one injurious utterance recruits an interlocked conflict network; whole-origin extraction prevents that network from obtaining acknowledged standing.

activation_trace.role: The bodily wound image recasts the word as an injury that can initiate effects beyond semantic content.
Entangled contention and mixed speech supply the branching social network through which the verbal wound spreads.
Corruption and association with bad companions supply recruitment of agents who sustain the dispute.
Extraction of the whole thing from its origin supplies dismantling of the network at its initiating injury.
Establishment and acknowledgment supply the standing that the contentious claim never secures.

changed_reading.before: The image concerns an intrinsically bad utterance with no endurance.
changed_reading.after: It can also diagnose an injurious utterance that grows by recruiting intertwined contention yet never acquires legitimate, settled standing.

context_deltas.mechanism: The expulsion threat, promised destruction, and counter-settlement turn the word-tree into a coercive order's claim over land. Its attempt to dislodge others rebounds as its own total removal, while the threatened group receives the habitation the speakers claimed as exclusively theirs.

activation_trace.role: Tree as origin supplies the collective stock or order whose territorial continuity is at issue.
Whole extraction from the origin supplies the reversal from threatened expulsion to removal of the threatening order.
The lower ground opposite the sky supplies the contested territorial substrate.
Settlement and fixity supply the tenure denied to the expelling order.
Passing out of a bounded place supplies the speakers' explicit mechanism of coercive expulsion.
Falling into destruction supplies the answering removal of the wrongdoers.
Taking a place as habitation supplies the counter-settlement granted after the removal.

structural_cues: 14:13 places a threat of expulsion from 'our land' immediately before the promised destruction of the wrongdoers.
14:14 reverses possession by settling the threatened group in the land after them.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: an expulsion claim is followed by destruction and counter-settlement. Reader arrow: the bad word is the territorial claim whose violence discloses its own lack of tenure. Live alternative: the sequence may describe regime succession without making the word itself the operative claim.

changed_reading.before: The uprooted tree represents generic moral instability.
changed_reading.after: It can represent an exclusionary order that says others have no place but, through that very claim, exposes its own possession of the land as uprootable.

context_deltas.mechanism: The lack of settlement becomes a failure to retain produced value: deliberate deeds are reduced to ash, violent air scatters them, and their makers lose effective possession of what they acquired. The bad word-tree is therefore not merely toppled; its whole output cannot be held.

activation_trace.role: The stemmed organism supplies an expected producer whose failure can be measured by what remains of its output.
Fixity supplies the missing retention mechanism linking production to durable possession.
Ash from burning supplies the valueless residue to which apparently substantial deeds are reduced.
A strong wind that lightens and scatters things supplies the transport that removes even the residue.
Effective capability and possession supply what the actors lack over the result of their deeds.
Seeking and obtaining benefit supplies the accumulated output that proves impossible to retain.

structural_cues: 14:18 is another explicit comparison and moves in one sentence from deeds to ash, wind, and inability over acquisition.
Both 14:18 and 14:26 end their images by negating a capacity to hold or remain.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: deeds become wind-scattered ash and cannot be controlled as acquisitions. Reader arrow: absence of قَرَارٍ names the same failure of retention in the word-tree. Live alternative: the ash image may remain a parallel judgment on deeds rather than an extension of the tree's mechanics.

changed_reading.before: The bad word lacks a place to stand.
changed_reading.after: It also lacks a retention system: whatever action or value gathers around it is rendered residue and dispersed beyond possession.

context_deltas.mechanism: The leader-follower scene and the later denial of coercive authority expose an uptake-dependent network. The bad word branches because hearers answer and align themselves with it, not because the utterance possesses intrinsic force; once call and response are separated under judgment, the network has no support.

activation_trace.role: Intelligible speech connecting speakers supplies the initiating relation between caller and respondent.
Entangled speech and contention supply the network shape created by repeated uptake.
Settlement supplies the independent support that the call-response network turns out not to possess.
Loyal following and succession supply the human branches attached to dominant speakers.
Power and governing authority supply the coercive force explicitly denied to the speaker.
Calling by speech supplies the only initiating action the speaker claims.
Answering speech supplies the hearers' contribution that completes and propagates the relation.

structural_cues: 14:21 stages followers seeking rescue from those they followed.
14:22 denies authority, reduces the mechanism to call and response, and then separates responsibility and rescue.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: hierarchy collapses into a non-coercive call answered by followers. Reader arrow: the tree's branches are social uptake events, so uprooting is disaggregation of that relation. Live alternative: 14:22 may be only a forensic allocation of blame, not an account of how bad speech grows.

changed_reading.before: The bad word fails because of an intrinsic defect.
changed_reading.after: Its apparent scale can be socially manufactured by answering, following hearers; without their uptake it has neither authority nor an independent root.

context_deltas.mechanism: The adjacent good-tree sequence provides a complete origin-to-output architecture: wholesome quality, base, fixity, elevated branch, recurring yield, and time. The bad word-tree is its process inverse, unable to preserve continuity from origin through extension to recurrent benefit.

activation_trace.role: Badness opposite wholesomeness marks both message and organism as the negative side of the paired architecture.
Whole-origin extraction supplies the direct reversal of a preserved base.
Negated fixity supplies the failure point from which extension and recurrent yield also become unavailable.
Wholesomeness explicitly opposed to badness supplies the matched positive quality of word and tree.
The origin and base supply the first stable stage of the good word's generative structure.
Durable fixity supplies the preserved connection between base and further growth.
A high branch emerging from an origin supplies legitimate extension rather than detached visibility.
The yield of tree and crop supplies concrete output from the preserved structure.
Recurring occasion supplies temporal reliability, extending stability beyond one visible moment.

structural_cues: 14:24 and 14:26 use matched word-tree syntax and repeat opposite quality adjectives across word and tree.
14:25 extends the positive image into recurrent yield before 14:26 removes the negative image's base and settlement.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: the positive tree explicitly has base, fixity, branch, and recurring yield; the negative tree is wholly extracted and has no settlement. Reader arrow: the negative image inversely fails the whole generative chain, not only the stated root stage. Live alternative: traits not explicitly negated in 14:26 should be treated as contrastive implications rather than direct predicates.

changed_reading.after: It is anti-generative: it cannot carry quality from a preserved origin into legitimate extension and recurrent benefit.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next ayah makes fixed speech the mediated means by which believers are stabilized. This transfers the spatial property of the word-tree into an effect on persons: a word with no settlement cannot furnish heart, mind, tongue, or life with durable orientation.

activation_trace.role: Intelligible speech connecting speakers supplies the discourse capable of orienting a hearer.
Negated settlement supplies the word's inability to confer a durable state.
Stability of heart, intellect, and tongue supplies the human faculties affected by fixed speech.
Speech as belief or doctrine supplies a durable orientation rather than a momentary vocal event.

structural_cues: 14:27 repeats ث ب ت as both governing verb and quality of القول.
The prepositional phrase with fixed speech mediates stabilization across present and later life.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: God is the stabilizing agent and fixed speech is the stated medium. Reader arrow: the focus word's missing قَرَارٍ is read through its failure to stabilize bearers. Live alternative: stabilization remains wholly divine, with speech an occasion rather than a causal instrument.

changed_reading.before: No settlement describes the word-tree itself.
changed_reading.after: No settlement also names what the bad word cannot give its bearers: durable orientation of belief, speech, and life.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later sequence moves from substituting disbelief for favor, to causing a people to lodge in ruin, to a condemned final settlement. The bad word-tree can therefore operate as a conversion pipeline: an ideological substitution reorganizes communal habitation, even though the word has no life-giving footing of its own.

activation_trace.role: A word widening into a saying or discourse supplies the ideological medium through which substitution can be normalized.
Negated settlement supplies the absence of viable present footing.
One thing taking the place of another supplies the initiating exchange of favor for disbelief.
Lodging in a place supplies the leaders' social effect of installing their people in a destination.
Ruin and corruption supply the quality of the habitation produced by the substitution.
Settlement reappears as the explicitly condemned destination, creating a temporal counterpoint to the focus denial.

structural_cues: 14:28 presents a causal sequence from substitution to causing a people to lodge in the abode of ruin.
14:29 closes that sequence with the same ق ر ر root used in 14:26, now as a condemned destination.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: value substitution leads to communal lodging in ruin and then to bad settlement. Reader arrow: the bad word is the discourse that mediates the substitution and reorganizes a people around it. Live alternative: the operative agents may be leaders and acts, while the word-tree remains only an adjacent analogy.

changed_reading.before: The bad word simply has no settlement.
changed_reading.after: It has no viable footing, yet it can route a community toward a ruinous terminal settlement; present rootlessness and final destination coexist.

context_deltas.mechanism: A later valley lacks cultivation yet receives settled descendants and a request for fruit. This weakens a purely ecological explanation of the bad tree: unproductive terrain does not by itself entail absence of habitation or hoped-for yield, so the focus failure lies more in the word-tree's quality and relations than in hostile soil.

activation_trace.role: Soft productive earth supplies the material condition whose absence might otherwise be blamed for the tree's failure.
Settlement supplies the outcome shown to remain possible even under ecological scarcity.
Taking a place as habitation supplies actual settlement in the explicitly non-cultivated valley.
Growing cultivation supplies the ecological capacity explicitly negated in the valley description.
Fruit as realized benefit supplies the requested output despite the valley's lack of cultivation.

structural_cues: 14:37 joins settled descendants, a valley explicitly lacking cultivation, ritual establishment, human inclination, and requested fruits.
The fruit is requested rather than reported, so the verse supports possibility and orientation more directly than realized harvest.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: habitation is placed in a non-cultivated valley and fruit is sought through relational and ritual orientation. Reader arrow: material barrenness alone cannot explain the focus tree's lack of settlement. Live alternative: the requested fruit is not yet an observed counterexample, so ecological dependence is weakened rather than discarded.

changed_reading.before: The tree's rootlessness could be explained mainly as failure of terrain or material conditions.
changed_reading.after: Even a barren setting can host settlement and oriented hope for fruit; the bad tree's failure is not reducible to its environment.

context_deltas.mechanism: A claim of never being removed is answered by former wrongdoers' dwellings, historical examples, and mountain-scale removability. The uprooted tree thus scales from one failed plant to a civilization's false permanence: occupation and apparent solidity are not the same as a secure origin.

activation_trace.role: Whole extraction supplies the concrete exposure of a permanence claim.
Fixity supplies the distinction between merely occupying a place and possessing durable settlement.
Removal from place or condition supplies the permanence that the speakers had sworn would not occur.
Dwelling in a habitation supplies apparent continuity while simultaneously placing occupants inside evidence of prior removal.
An example as lesson and sign supplies historical comparison that should puncture the claim of permanence.
Removal recurs at mountain scale, supplying an upper bound for what apparent solidity can guarantee.
A high solid mass supplies the strongest visible counterimage to the uprooted tree and is itself placed under possible movement.

structural_cues: 14:44 recalls an explicit oath of no removal.
14:45 places the speakers in prior wrongdoers' dwellings and says examples were given; 14:46 then invokes mountains and removal.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: asserted permanence is surrounded by inherited ruins, examples, and mountain-scale removal. Reader arrow: the word-tree is a political-civilizational permanence claim exposed as surface occupation without secure origin. Live alternative: the mountain clause may measure the enormity of plotting without identifying the plotters with the tree.

changed_reading.before: The uprooted plant is a small-scale image of weak falsehood.
changed_reading.after: It can expose even inherited dwellings, regimes, and mountain-like structures as surface permanence unsupported by a durable origin.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it reads the comparison as an enacted public penalty rather than only a verbal simile. It remains anchored in the punishment-as-example branch of م ث ل, the passive whole extraction, exposure above ground, and the later use of examples as warning. Downstream prose should label it a juridical or demonstrative overlay, not the default sense of مَثَلُ.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: مَثَلُ at word 1, ٱجْتُثَّتْ at word 6, and فَوْقِ ٱلْأَرْضِ at words 8-9 present an extracted object that can be seen as a warning display.

activation_trace.role: Punishment that makes the punished one an example supplies the deterrent function of the uprooted object.
Whole extraction from the origin supplies the enacted penalty rather than a merely verbal judgment.
Spatial elevation above the ground supplies visibility for the negative exhibit.
Example as lesson and sign supplies the later warning function that keeps the punitive reading live.

changed_reading.before: The verse offers a comparison describing bad speech.
changed_reading.after: The extracted tree can also be carried as a public negative example whose exposed condition warns other claimants.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it joins one tree's lack of footing to the later replacement of the entire earth. It remains anchored in the focus emphasis on being above the earth with no settlement and in 14:48's explicit substitution of one earth for another. Downstream prose should present it as an eschatological scale-shift, not as proof that 14:26 directly predicts 14:48.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: فَوْقِ ٱلْأَرْضِ and مَا لَهَا مِن قَرَارٍۢ make the bad word-tree radically dependent on a ground it does not securely inhabit.

activation_trace.role: Dominance from above supplies an apparent sovereignty that remains external to the supporting ground.
The ground below supplies the substrate on which the word-tree's apparent presence depends.
Absent fixity supplies the inability to survive a change in substrate.
One thing standing in place of another supplies replacement of the whole supporting ground.
The repeated earth names the old and replacement substrates across which unsupported sovereignty cannot persist.
Overwhelming conquest from above supplies the genuine sovereignty before which merely surface-level dominance is displaced.

changed_reading.before: The bad word-tree lacks stable soil in the present image.
changed_reading.after: Its apparent above-ground sovereignty is so substrate-dependent that it cannot persist when the ground itself is replaced.

strongest_changes: The expulsion and counter-settlement sequence turns uprooting into a reversal of territorial coercion.
The adjacent good tree makes the bad tree a failure of the whole origin-to-branch-to-recurring-yield process.
Fixed speech stabilizing believers transfers botanical settlement into durable orientation of human bearers.
The later move from substituted value to communal ruin and bad settlement creates a temporal counterpoint to the focus tree's lack of settlement.
The call-response scene reveals that a bad word's apparent branching can depend on hearer uptake rather than intrinsic authority.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah context repeatedly re-scaled one uprooted word-tree across bodily injury, social uptake, territorial tenure, retained output, personal stabilization, communal habitation, historical permanence, and finally the replaceability of the ground itself, while each retained model remained attached to focus words and constructions.
remaining_uncertainties: The full inversion of the good tree's fruit and timing is structurally strong but extends beyond properties explicitly negated in 14:26.
The recurrence of ق ر ر in 14:29 may deliberately distinguish viable present footing from a condemned final destination, or it may simply juxtapose separate uses.
The territorial, political, and uptake mechanisms require reader-supplied arrows from narrative sequence to the word-tree and should remain distinguishable from the direct botanical contrast.
The wound-dispute model is well anchored in branch inventories but remains form-distant from the immediate nominal reading of كَلِمَةٍ and شَجَرَةٍ.
